title: Achilles and the rotor

data.source: Zeno behaviour in hybrid dynamical systems and the dwell-time condition that excludes it (Johansson, Egerstedt, Lygeros and Sastry 1999; Zhang, Johansson, Lygeros and Sastry 2001; cited from memory). Checked numerically here. Adapted from colloquy/lab/metaphysical/open_points_and_zeno.py.

phoenix_status: MATHEMATICS.md section IV: "The positive lower bound on `T_n` rules out infinitely many cuts in finite time. This is a standard hybrid-ODE argument; it does not prove objective openness." Section V: "three contents `(0,0,pi)` with `q=(sqrt(5)-1)/2` put equal total weight at `0` and `pi`; the two means `pi/2` and `3pi/2` tie. This algebraic `q` is a counterexample, not a prediction of a golden-ratio constant." Section VII (ONTOLOGY): "An entirely deterministic R4 can still fix its future uniquely."
prediction: Without the bound, endlessly many occasions fit in a finite time; with it they do not; and the printed tie is a tie.
baseline: The theorem itself: Zeno behaviour of hybrid systems and the dwell-time condition (cited from memory). Decoy: a plain geometric series.
why: Drop the bound on the drive and endlessly many occasions fit inside a finite time (9.502 time units for a thousand, 9.505 for a million). Keep the bound and a thousand times more occasions take about a thousand times longer. That is the standard Zeno behaviour of hybrid systems and its standard cure, so "finite becoming" is put in by the bounds. The printed tie is a tie, for every q. Two of the lens's five predictions were wrong as written and are kept.
